speaker: Amit Shah
venue: Lok Sabha, debate on statutory resolution confirming President's Rule in Manipur
quote_english: The situation is in control. There has been no death in the last four months. I won't say the situation is satisfactory.
summary: Shah said Manipur was under control with no deaths in four months, but press reports document at least three violence-linked deaths in Manipur between mid-December 2024 and 8 March 2025.

analysis:
On 3 April 2025, in the Lok Sabha debate confirming President's Rule, Shah said the Manipur situation was under control with no deaths in the previous four months, while adding it was not satisfactory because displaced people were still in relief camps. He gave an overall figure of about 260 deaths since May 2023, 80 percent of them in the first month (Business Standard).

The Wire reports specific killings after the start of that period: two Bihar migrant workers in Kakching on 14 December 2024 and one man in Kangpokpi on 8 March 2025, plus earlier deaths in November 2024. Police described the Kakching case as unsolved. The Quint fact-check rated the claim misleading, citing seven instances of deaths since December.

Some counted deaths are disputed in cause (relief-camp deaths attributed by Kuki groups to medical neglect), and the government's own definition of 'violence-related' death was not found. At least the three killings in specific incidents fall within the four-month window, so the 'no death' statement is not supported by press reports. The 'under control' judgement is an assessment, not a testable figure.
notes: Shah's exact Hindi wording not found; English from The Tribune. The Wire says Shah repeated 'no violence since November' in the Rajya Sabha on 4 April 2025. The Quint page returned 403 so its detail is from a search summary only. Quint publication date not confirmed. No official Manipur Police fatality list was found. Earlier Shah statements on Manipur in 2023 (29 May visit, 9 Aug 2023 no-confidence speech) were checked only for wording; no 'under control' quote found for those dates.
